origin.description: A queue backed by a list used as a ring. The list grows by doubling and shrinks when at most a quarter of it is occupied, never below init.

arguments.name: init
arguments.text: Initial and minimum length of the backing list.

arguments.name: missing_default
arguments.text: Value returned by remove() or peek() when the queue is empty. The default is NULL.

origin.details: add and madd append. remove and mremove take from the front and return the objects oldest first. peek does not remove. as_list runs from oldest to newest. An empty mremove stops with a zero-length replacement.
origin.value: A list of functions closing over the queue.
origin.example: q <- fastqueue(3); q$add(1); q$add(2); q$add(3); q$add(4); q$as_list(); q$remove()

translation.description: A queue backed by a list used as a ring. Capacity doubles and shrinks when at most a quarter is occupied, never below init.

arguments.name: init
arguments.text: Initial and minimum length of the backing list.

arguments.name: missing_default
arguments.text: Value returned by remove() or peek() when the queue is empty. The default is None.

translation.details: add and madd append. madd's _list is R's .list and is appended after the positional objects. remove and mremove take from the front. An empty mremove raises ValueError.
translation.value: A FastQueue. Call methods with Python syntax.
translation.example:
from fastmap.fastqueue import fastqueue
q = fastqueue(3)
q.add(1); q.add(2); q.add(3); q.add(4)
print(q.as_list()); print(q.remove())
